subject.title: fix(agents): skip error classification for clean non-zero exits

question: Should normally exited non-zero commands remain warning-worthy by default, or should exec gain an explicit accepted-exit semantic that callers can opt into?
rationale: The runtime's `completed` status only means normal process termination, so distinguishing an expected no-match from a genuine failed command requires an explicit product contract rather than this classifier inference.

options.title: Require explicit accepted exits
options.body: Preserve current non-zero warning behavior and add a narrowly defined result or invocation signal for intentionally accepted exit codes.

options.title: Keep current behavior
options.body: Retain all non-zero warnings and close the linked request as unsupported unless commands normalize expected exits themselves.

options.title: Suppress all normal exits
options.body: Accept that genuine commands exiting 1–125 will no longer produce automatic channel failure warnings.

recommendation.title: Require explicit accepted exits
recommendation.body: Preserve current non-zero warning behavior and add a narrowly defined result or invocation signal for intentionally accepted exit codes.
